statement: Largest known training run >= 5e27 FLOP (Epoch AI; by 2027-12-31)
status_at_phase_end: Far from met in 2023. The largest publicly estimated run in-phase was the March 2023 frontier model at roughly 2e25 FLOP (third-party estimate; developer did not disclose compute) - about 250x below the threshold. A larger multimodal model launched in December without disclosed compute. Bloc A's 1e26 reporting threshold was set above any known run.

items.summary: Following the March 2023 frontier-model release, a forecaster's retrospective cited the Epoch AI estimate of its training compute at about 2.2e25 FLOP, the largest known run at the time; compute was not disclosed by the developer.
items.detail: LessWrong, Stephen McAleese, 'Retrospective on GPT-4 Predictions After the Release of GPT-4', posted 2023-03-17, citing EpochAI visualization (GPT-4 ~2.2e25 FLOP). The Epoch figure is visible in the search snippet but not in the extracted head; the post may have been edited after posting, so the as-of status of the figure is uncertain.

items.summary: A top-5 developer launched its 'largest and most capable' multimodal model family, claiming the top variant was the first to beat human experts on a major knowledge benchmark (90.0%); training compute was not disclosed.
items.detail: Google, 'Introducing Gemini: our largest and most capable AI model', 2023-12-06; Gemini Ultra MMLU 90.0%. (Later third-party compute estimates are outside the phase and not used.)

items.summary: Bloc A set its interim frontier-model reporting threshold at 1e26 operations - above any publicly known 2023 run and still 50x below this indicator's 5e27 threshold.
The frontier developer's system card and technical report gave no training-compute figures, so in-phase compute for the largest runs rested on third-party estimates only.
items.detail: OpenAI GPT-4 System Card (no compute disclosed; 'finished training in August of 2022').
